entries.market_reading: The investor wants the cash amount paid or declared per share, usually annualised, and whether it has been rising, flat or falling. 'Raised' or 'cut' is always measured against the company's own prior declared rate, not against other companies.

figures.name: dividends declared per common share
figures.notes: 10-Q facts exist for both the 3-month quarter and the year-to-date; select by duration length. DividendsPayableAmountPerShare is an instant (a declared, unpaid amount). Per-class values sit on us-gaap:StatementClassOfStockAxis.

figures.name: dividends declared, aggregate (equity statement)
figures.notes: Declared basis. DividendsCommonStock and Dividends include dividends settled in stock and payment-in-kind (PIK) as well as cash, and Dividends and DividendsCash can include preferred dividends. For a cash dividend history use DividendsCommonStockCash, then DividendsCash less preferred dividends. Do not use DividendsCommonStock or Dividends in a year that has a stock dividend.

entries.formula: Annual dividend per share = the per-share amounts declared for the four most recent quarters added together (or the fiscal-year per-share figure). Growth = this year's annual amount divided by last year's, minus one. A raise or cut = the latest regular declared rate compared with the previous regular rate, after split adjustment.
entries.period_convention: Latest fiscal year or the four most recently declared quarters for the level; year over year and 3-5 years for growth; the previous declaration for 'raised' or 'cut'.
entries.frame_notes: History: the company's own prior rate and multi-year record decide 'raised', 'cut', 'fast' or 'slow' growth. Peers: only growth rates are compared across companies; the level of dividend per share means nothing across companies without price (yield, SH-06) or earnings (payout, SH-02).
entries.direction: depends: a rising dividend reads as positive only when earnings and free cash flow cover it (SH-02, SH-03)

pitfalls: Declared versus paid: the amount declared in a quarter can differ from the cash paid in that quarter because record and payment dates straddle quarter ends; keep one basis.
Year-to-date 10-Q facts added to quarterly facts double-count; pick facts by duration length.
Stock splits: per-share amounts filed before a split are on the old share basis; use the latest filing's restated comparatives or divide by the cumulative split ratio (SH-22).
Special or one-time dividends inflate one year; they are usually identified in text or with a company-specific member, not a separate standard element, so separate them before computing growth.
Share classes can carry different dividends; read per-class facts rather than a single company-level value.
The 10-K dividend history table no longer exists (Item 201(c)(1) reserved since 2018); history comes from the S-X 3-04 equity analysis and XBRL facts.
Foreign private issuers report dividends in their own currency and per ordinary share; the per-ADS amount depends on the ADS ratio and exchange rates.
Structured data begins in 2009-2011 depending on filer size; earlier history needs the filing text.

entries.market_reading: The share of profit paid out as dividends. A high payout leaves little room to keep the dividend if earnings fall, and a payout above 100% means dividends exceed earnings. 'High' is judged against the company's own history and its industry, not against a universal number.

figures.name: diluted earnings per share
figures.notes: Use the same period and share basis as the dividend figure.

figures.name: aggregate method: common dividends and earnings to common
figures.notes: If only NetIncomeLoss is available, subtract preferred dividends (us-gaap:DividendsPreferredStock or us-gaap:PreferredStockDividendsIncomeStatementImpact).

entries.formula: Payout ratio = dividends declared per common share divided by diluted earnings per share for the same period (or common dividends divided by net income available to common shareholders). Coverage = the inverse (earnings divided by dividends). Retention ratio = one minus the payout ratio.
entries.period_convention: Latest fiscal year or trailing twelve months; compare with the company's own 3-5 year average and with the prior year.
entries.frame_notes: History: 'high' = well above the company's own multi-year payout. Peers: well above its industry's typical payout; industry payout tables (e.g. Damodaran's sector data, January 2026) are practitioner corroboration, not authority. Absolute: only the definitional lines (payout above 100%, and loss years where the ratio is not meaningful).
entries.direction: depends: a lower payout means more cushion and more reinvestment; a higher payout returns more cash but with less margin; mature, regulated and pass-through businesses (REITs, utilities, MLPs, BDCs) run structurally higher payouts

thresholds.line: payout ratio > 100% (earnings coverage < 1.0x)
thresholds.meaning: Dividends exceed earnings for the period; the excess is funded from cash, borrowing or asset sales.

thresholds.line: earnings per share <= 0
thresholds.meaning: The payout ratio is negative or undefined and should be reported as 'dividend paid despite a loss', never as a low payout.

thresholds.line: earnings coverage above 2.0x (payout below about 50%)
thresholds.meaning: Wall Street Prep's rule of thumb (a training provider, not an authoritative line): it presents earnings coverage of 2.0x as the minimum 'floor' before holders should be concerned about sustainability. It does not fit REITs, utilities or MLPs.

GAAP net income includes one-offs (impairments, gains on sale); a single year can spike. Company-defined adjusted earnings are not citable figures for the desk.

entries.market_reading: Whether the cash the business generates after capital spending covers the cash dividend. A payout on free cash flow above 100% means the dividend is being funded from cash reserves, borrowing or asset sales.

figures.name: cash dividends paid to common holders
figures.sign: reported as a positive number for an outflow (credit-balance element)
figures.notes: 10-Q cash-flow values are fiscal year-to-date; derive a quarter or trailing twelve months by differencing (TTM = latest FY + current YTD - prior-year YTD). PaymentsOfDividends includes preferred dividends and distributions to noncontrolling interests. Use it only when PaymentsOfDividendsCommonStock is absent, and subtract PaymentsOfDividendsMinorityInterest and preferred dividends (PaymentsOfDividendsPreferredStockAndPreferenceStock) where they are tagged.

figures.name: operating cash flow
figures.notes: 10-Q cash-flow values are fiscal year-to-date; derive a quarter or trailing twelve months by differencing (TTM = latest FY + current YTD - prior-year YTD).

figures.name: capital expenditures
figures.notes: 10-Q cash-flow values are fiscal year-to-date; derive a quarter or trailing twelve months by differencing (TTM = latest FY + current YTD - prior-year YTD). Use the cash-flow family's capex definition.

entries.formula: Free-cash-flow payout = cash dividends paid to common holders divided by (operating cash flow minus capital expenditures). Cash coverage = the inverse.
entries.period_convention: Trailing twelve months or latest fiscal year; 3-5 year sums are common because capital spending is lumpy.
entries.frame_notes: Absolute: above 100% = not covered by free cash flow (definitional). History: a rising cash payout versus the company's own record. Peers: industry cash-return ratios (Damodaran's net cash returned / FCFE, practitioner) as corroboration.
entries.direction: lower is safer; above 100% means the dividend was not covered by free cash flow in that period

thresholds.line: free-cash-flow payout > 100%
thresholds.meaning: Dividends paid exceed free cash flow; the gap was funded by cash on hand, debt or asset sales.

thresholds.line: free cash flow <= 0
thresholds.meaning: The ratio is not meaningful; every dollar of dividend came from other sources.

entries.market_reading: A forward-looking judgement assembled from filed facts: coverage by earnings and by free cash flow and their trend, balance-sheet capacity against obligations, legal or contractual limits on paying dividends, sector rules, and management's own stated intention. Filings supply the evidence and the lines that apply; they never certify 'safe'.

figures.name: earnings payout and free-cash-flow payout
figures.notes: Not in us-gaap/dei/ecd XBRL: see SH-02 and SH-03.

figures.name: restrictions on dividends (text)
figures.notes: Not in us-gaap/dei/ecd XBRL: no standard numeric element; S-X 4-08(e) note and Form 8-K Item 3.03. Amounts of restricted or unrestricted retained earnings are disclosed in the note when material.

entries.formula: No single formula. Assemble: (1) earnings payout and its trend; (2) free-cash-flow payout and its trend; (3) leverage and liquidity against obligations (debt maturities, capital commitments); (4) any disclosed restriction on dividends and covenant headroom; (5) sector rules (bank payout limits tied to capital buffers; REIT distribution requirement); (6) management's stated dividend intention.
entries.period_convention: Trailing twelve months and latest fiscal year with a 3-5 year trend; bank payout limits are set each quarter from the previous quarter-end buffer.
entries.frame_notes: History: coverage deteriorating over several periods. Peers: payout well above the industry norm. Obligations: dividends plus debt service and committed capex against cash generation and liquidity (MD&A capital resources discussion). Absolute: the definitional 100% lines, plus sector regulatory lines (bank maximum payout ratio; REIT 90% distribution requirement).
entries.direction: depends: lower payout, positive and rising coverage, modest leverage and no binding restriction read as safer

thresholds.line: bank capital conservation buffer at or below 2.5% (plus any countercyclical buffer)
thresholds.meaning: A Federal Reserve-regulated banking organization becomes subject to a maximum payout ratio on distributions and discretionary bonuses: 60%, 40%, 20% or 0% of eligible retained income as the buffer falls through the Table 1 bands; firms subject to a stress capital buffer use their own buffer requirement.

thresholds.line: REIT dividends-paid deduction at least 90% of REIT taxable income
thresholds.meaning: A REIT must distribute at least this share of taxable income (excluding net capital gain) to keep REIT tax treatment, so part of a REIT dividend is a legal requirement and GAAP payout above 100% is normal.

thresholds.line: payout above 100% of earnings or of free cash flow
thresholds.meaning: Not covered by that measure in the period (see SH-02, SH-03).

thresholds.line: any missed preferred dividend since the last audited fiscal year-end
thresholds.meaning: The company loses Form S-3 eligibility; a filed consequence of dividend stress on preferred stock.

pitfalls: 'Safe' is a judgement: present the evidence and the lines that apply, never a verdict the desk cannot cite.
Bank limits differ by firm: large holding companies use a stress capital buffer in place of the fixed 2.5% (12 CFR 217.11(c)); the buffer inputs are in regulatory reports, not the 10-K alone.
REIT payout on GAAP EPS is misleading; the market uses FFO/AFFO (Nareit definitions, tier 2, covered by the REIT family) and taxable income.

Covenant restrictions sit in credit agreements (exhibits) and are summarised under S-X 4-08(e) in annual statements; interim reports may not repeat them, so absence in a 10-Q is not evidence of no restriction.
Management 'intends to continue' statements are encouraged, not required (Item 201(c)(2)); silence is not a signal either way.
A dividend funded by new borrowing shows as debt proceeds alongside dividend payments in financing cash flows; read both.
entries.notes: no_market_threshold is true: no authoritative line decides whether a dividend is 'safe' (Research: 'safe' has no agreed test). The sector lines here are owner-specific, each drawn for its own purpose and shown with its owner: the Federal Reserve capital rule's maximum payout ratio (banks), the tax code's 90% REIT distribution requirement, and Form S-3's missed-preferred-dividend condition. None is a market line for 'safe'.

entries.market_reading: A split changes the number of shares and the per-share price proportionally without changing ownership; a reverse split does the opposite, often to meet an exchange's minimum bid price. Adjusted historical count = old count times the product of the oriented ratios of every split after that date. Adjusted per-share amount = old amount divided by that product. notes: How to read this family. (1) Source ids are stable across entries (e.g. SK703 = 17 CFR 229.703); a source object repeats in every entry that uses it with an entry-specific 'supports'. PD quotes were each checked as exact substrings of the text fetched in this run and are 25 words or fewer. (2) no_market_threshold is true when no authoritative source draws a line that makes the figure 'low' or 'high'. Procedural lines (filing deadlines, disclosure triggers, safe-harbor conditions) are still listed under thresholds as 'source-drawn' but do not by themselves set no_market_threshold to false; it is false only where a rule defines a size or level (bank payout limits and the REIT distribution requirement in SH-04; the exchange 20% rules in SH-21; the 5%/10%/20% ownership lines in SH-27 and SH-28). (3) Much of this family is not in us-gaap XBRL: Item 703 monthly repurchase tables, beneficial-ownership tables, 8-K Item 3.02 details, prospectus terms and holders of record are text; Form 4, Form 13F and (since 18 Dec 2024) Schedules 13D/13G are separate structured XML documents; Item 408(a) and pay-versus-performance TSR are tagged in the ecd taxonomy. (4) Rules in force changed recently and the dates matter for history: the 2023 daily share-repurchase rule was vacated (19 Dec 2023; CFR restored 8 Apr 2024); 13D/13G deadlines shortened from 5 Feb 2024 (13G from 30 Sep 2024; XML from 18 Dec 2024); Form 4 10b5-1 checkbox from 1 Apr 2023; Form 13F values in dollars from 3 Jan 2023 (thousands before); Section 16 reporting for foreign private issuers' directors and officers from 18 Mar 2026; Rule 13f-2 / Form SHO exempted until 2 Jan 2028. (5) Pending SEC proposals as of 24 Sep 2026 that would move lines in this family if adopted: Registered Offering Reform (91 FR 31022; would drop the $75 million S-3 float test and widen WKSI benefits), filer-status simplification (91 FR 30086; would change the Item 3.02 5% category and public-float filer lines), optional semiannual reporting on Form 10-S (91 FR 24968; would change the cadence of quarterly items such as Item 703 and Item 408(a) for opting companies), and proxy and Rule 14a-8 changes (91 FR 59852, 91 FR 59904). Re-check adoption before relying on the current lines. (6) Rule 4 reminder: the configured finance server's insiderTrades, form13F and secFilings endpoints are redistributors: leads for finding, never cited; every figure here must be re-derived from the filing. (7) Element observations (switches between PaymentsOfDividends and PaymentsOfDividendsCommonStock; us-gaap to srt move of the repurchase-authorization element; TreasuryStockShares and the day-month-year dividend payment-date element absent from 2026 us-gaap) come from the project's own SEC fixtures and the FASB 2026 taxonomy files; element names are identifiers only (licence OD), and no FASB documentation text is stored.
